```{r data-generation, echo=FALSE, results="hide"}
library(exams)
vehicles <- 9
weekly_mean <- 3.5
not_rented <- 3
a <- dpois(vehicles - not_rented, weekly_mean)
b <- 4 * weekly_mean
pair <- function(x, y) sprintf("(a) %.4f; (b) %.1f", x, y)
answers <- c(pair(a, b), pair(ppois(vehicles - not_rented, weekly_mean), b),
  pair(dpois(not_rented, weekly_mean), b),
  pair(dpois(vehicles, weekly_mean), weekly_mean))
solutions <- c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE)
ord <- sample(seq_along(answers))
answers <- answers[ord]
solutions <- solutions[ord]
```

Question
========

A motorhome rental company owns `r vehicles` vehicles. During summer, weekly demand follows a Poisson distribution with mean `r sprintf("%.1f", weekly_mean)` and is independent from week to week.

(a) What is the probability that exactly `r not_rented` vehicles are not rented in one week?  
(b) What is the expected demand over four weeks?

Choose the pair containing the two correct answers.

```{r question-list, echo=FALSE, results="asis"}
answerlist(answers, markup = "markdown")
```

Solution
========

For (a), demand must equal $`r vehicles`-`r not_rented`=`r vehicles - not_rented`$, giving `r sprintf("%.4f", a)`. For (b), expected demand over four weeks is $4\times `r sprintf("%.1f", weekly_mean)`=`r sprintf("%.1f", b)`$.

================

exsolution: `r mchoice2string(solutions)`
